clue.text: Flipping pickpocket circling queen in old building

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
circling means going round, so the pickpocket's letters surround the queen's

parts.note: to dip is to pick pockets, and a dip is a pickpocket
Mary is the name of several English and Scottish queens

explanation.surface: A thief doing somersaults around a monarch inside some ancient monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' applies to the whole container, not just the pickpocket: build first, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The pyramids of Egypt are among the most famous ancient structures, so an old building fits.

clue.text: Old Testament book, small relief when under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming below, so the pressure letter goes on top

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
alms are charitable gifts to relieve the poor

explanation.surface: A book of scripture offers a little comfort when times are stressful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Psalms is a collection of sacred songs in the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Feast on starter of guacamole before beer

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, here of guacamole

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone dines on a dip as a first course followed by a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feast on' looks like the definition, but 'on' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain them lavishly with food, so it means to feast them.

clue.text: Dressing up in dungarees I annoy Americans

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards
in means contained within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone getting dressed in work overalls irritates people from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a sauce used to dress salads, so it is a dressing.

clue.text: Nationality of wife

definitions.meaning: The nationality of people from the Netherlands
in Cockney usage 'my old ...' means my wife, from duchess

explanation.surface: Asking where one's wife comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' for wife is old London slang, short for 'duchess', as in the music-hall song 'My Old Dutch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch names people of the Netherlands, and in Cockney slang a man's wife.

clue.text: Type of humour golf provides

parts.note: Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
allows, in the sense of grants or provides for

explanation.surface: A remark that the game of golf is a source of a particular comic style.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallows humour is grim joking about death or disaster, so the word names that kind of comedy.

clue.text: Diver having shameful feeling gobbling fruit endlessly

indicators.note: gobbling means eating up greedily, so the first word swallows the other

parts.note: guilt is the feeling of shame at wrongdoing

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the fruit drops its last letter

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A swimmer stuffs himself with fruit while feeling guilty about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' is a bird here, not a person: several seabirds are called divers for how they hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: Musical instrument Rob picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is identified by how it sounds

parts.note: to loot is to rob or plunder

explanation.surface: A thief lifts a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a plucked string instrument with a rounded back, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Sleek quality of old island cat, expressing love

indicators.note: expressing means squeezing out, as juice from fruit, so a letter is pressed out of the cat

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, as on maps
a lioness is a big cat
love means zero in tennis scoring, and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: An elderly island cat with a glossy coat is affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' squeezes love's O out of the cat, not out of the old O at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiliness is the slick, smooth character of something greasy, so it is a sleek quality.

clue.text: Outside it is sensible to clean up

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the word for sensible wraps round the other words

parts.note: sane means sensible or rational

explanation.surface: Advice that tidying up outdoors is the wise thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanitise is to clean something thoroughly, especially to disinfect it.

clue.text: Furious with some receiving tips from gangster

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the word for some holds the other letters

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any?'

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, here of gangster

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged when a few of them are given something by a mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious and angry are synonyms, both describing strong rage.

clue.text: Sporting event in North Italy cut short surprisingly

indicators.note: something turning out surprisingly comes out in an unexpected form, so the letters are rearranged
cut short means losing its end, so Italy drops its last letter

explanation.surface: An athletics contest staged in the north of Italy was unexpectedly curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims ITALY to ITAL; 'surprisingly' rearranges NORTH plus ITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is a sports race combining swimming, cycling and running.

clue.text: Am lonely travelling round Switzerland, becoming depressed

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go about the country code
travelling means moving about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A solitary traveller touring the Alps confesses to feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges AM LONELY into MELANOLY; 'round' puts it around CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Melancholy is a deep sadness, so as an adjective it means low-spirited or gloomy.

clue.text: Defeat overturned in tie

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so the word for defeat is read backwards

parts.note: tonk is informal for thrash or beat heavily

explanation.surface: A loss reversed on appeal ends up as a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses TONK, informal British slang for beating someone soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie a cord is to knot it, so the noun for a fastening fits.

clue.text: Swore Sam helped out after introduction of bonuses

indicators.note: after means following, so the shuffled letters come after the single letter
the introduction of a word is its first letter, here of bonuses
out means disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sam cursed after helping and then the bonus scheme came in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SAM HELPED; 'after' places it behind the B.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to speak profanely, so blasphemed means cursed.

clue.text: Space, following student requests, for hot-drink dispensers

parts.note: a vacuum is a space empty of matter
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
L for learner, the plate on a learner driver's car
asks means requests

explanation.surface: Room is made after pupils ask for something to serve hot drinks from.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuum flasks keep tea or coffee hot and are poured from, so they serve as drink dispensers.

clue.text: Dangerous line a French PM adopts, foolhardy ultimately

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the prime minister's name takes in the letter

parts.note: Edward Heath was a British prime minister in the 1970s

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of foolhardy is taken

explanation.surface: A reckless policy taken up by a prime minister from France proves risky.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was UK prime minister from 1970 to 1974; 'adopts' puts L inside HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhealthy means harmful to health, so it can mean hazardous or dangerous.

clue.text: Without people to fill rugby union team

indicators.note: to fill means to go inside, so the people word sits within the other

parts.note: sans means without
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A rugby side short of players needs to recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Saracens is a rugby union club based in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracens is a professional English rugby union club, so it is a team.

clue.text: Haughty supporter of King Charles?

definitions.meaning: the ... were Royalists who backed Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.surface: A query about an arrogant follower of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The English Civil War (1642-51) pitted King Charles I's Cavaliers against Parliament's Roundheads.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalier means disdainfully offhand, and was the name for Royalist followers of Charles I.

clue.text: Someone who's proficient with numbers?

parts.note: numbers here are not figures but things that numb; this doctor is skilled with drugs that remove sensation

explanation.surface: Seemingly about a mathematician or accountant good with figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'numbers' as 'numb-ers', agents that make you numb.
explanation.definitionFit: This hospital doctor administers anaesthetics, the drugs that deaden pain during surgery.

clue.text: Prior to failure clubs would get more miserly

indicators.note: prior to means before, so the card-suit letter comes first

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
a loser is a failure

explanation.surface: Golf clubs that keep failing would become stingier.
explanation.definitionFit: Close means tight-fisted with money, so the comparative means stingier.

clue.text: Urge son to describe outwardly dirty, revolting city

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the whole assembled string is read backwards
to describe means to draw round, so the outer letters enclose the others

parts.note: a yen is a longing or urge

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the two end letters of dirty are taken

explanation.surface: A boy is urged to portray a filthy, disgusting city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like a description of the city, but it reverses everything built before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney is the largest city in Australia.

clue.text: Was weary from time to time on holiday

indicators.note: from time to time means occasionally, so only every other letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone occasionally felt tired while on a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone away from work or home on a trip is on holiday.

clue.text: Cheese from Chile mostly player ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a set arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means most but not all, so Chile drops its last letter

explanation.surface: A sportsman requests a cheese imported from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CHILE to CHIL; 'ordered' rearranges CHIL plus PLAYER.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a crumbly white Welsh cheese named after a town in Wales.

clue.text: Cleric fails to finish page of book

indicators.note: failing to finish means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A priest never gets to the end of a page of his book.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf.

clue.text: Sticks around being self-righteous

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for sticks is read backwards

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

explanation.surface: Someone sticking around is acting holier-than-thou.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug means complacently pleased with oneself, close to a self-righteous attitude.

clue.text: Origin of cake I'm eating somehow is obscure

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged
the origin of a word is its first letter, here of cake

explanation.surface: How a piece of cake ends up in someone's mouth is a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is the adverb after 'eating', so the cake's first letter stays outside the shuffle and goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enigmatic is puzzling and hard to interpret, so it is mysterious or unclear.

clue.text: Stonecutter, one evicted from French home

indicators.note: evicted means thrown out of a property, so a letter is removed from the house word

parts.note: maison is French for house or home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A craftsman is turned out of a house in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason is a craftsman who cuts and dresses stone for building.

clue.text: Thin head of gym during yoga regularly bends back

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the whole assembled string is read in reverse
during means in the middle of, so one letter sits inside the others
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of yoga is taken
the head of a word is its first letter, here of gym

parts.note: arcs are curves or bends

explanation.surface: A gaunt gym leader stretching backwards during a yoga class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses everything before it, not only the bends; 'regularly' takes the odd letters of yoga.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraggy describes a lean, bony body, so it means skinny.

clue.text: Well-behaved hospital worker

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means disciplined and well-conducted
a hospital attendant doing non-medical tasks

explanation.surface: Praise for a disciplined member of the hospital staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means tidy and disciplined, and is also the title of a hospital attendant.
